Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

NNS 13.3 (development changes)

CRAN release: 2026-10-30

Statistical targets and interpretation

  • Preserve the distinction between frequency probabilities (degree zero), directional deviation-area shares (positive degrees), and their induced laws. Correct one-sided probability bounds, divergent-moment labels, finite-moment conditions, prediction-interval claims, and the scope of dependence/causation.
  • ANOVA retains its separate mean, median, and distribution-profile targets. Median comparisons now handle CDF jumps, and degenerate area-balance cases use explicit agreement semantics. Certainty remains a descriptive score; inferential calibration must match the target and sampling design.
  • NNS.FSD(type = "continuous") keeps the same numerical degree-one criterion but labels it Omega/expectile order. Its result strings now use OMEGA, not FSD; callers comparing strings should update. Discrete FSD strings and numeric dominance indicators/set/cluster structures are unchanged.

Regression, classification, and derivatives

  • NNS.reg and NNS.stack accept type = "REG" to select numeric regression explicitly. Forecasting, derivative, and hazard-smoothing helpers use this contract even when a response has only two values; they retain fractional predictions on the original scale.
  • Nominal classification retains class probabilities in predictor cells and combines those probabilities before choosing labels. Numeric class labels are not interpolation coordinates. Probability outputs and descriptive prediction sets expose the target; factor/character output codes use class.levels.
  • Binary numeric coordinates retain distinct terminal cells in both R and native regression paths, including dummy columns in mixed predictor designs.
  • Stack’s multivariate component searches selected predictor coordinates; its dimension-reduction component separately uses the synthetic index. Complexity selection uses both response orientations without changing the underlying directional statistics. These corrections can change fitted predictions.
  • Distance kernels use consistent exponential rates and sample rank scales across scalar, bulk, and parallel paths. Partial derivatives use admissible local support and explicit boundary differences. Unsupported multivariate NNS.CDF(type = "hazard") requests now fail instead of returning CDF/survival as if it were density/survival.
  • Stack’s multivariate component keeps the same coordinates in every fold, so a predictor that is constant in one fold no longer stops the search. A declared factor level with no training rows is a valid test value, a single test row with a factor predictor is accepted, and categorical NNS.reg honours an explicit n.best.
  • Nominal classification reuses each fold’s cells and sorted distances for every neighbour count and skips fitted classes in point-only calls. It is still slower than the former class-code regression: for three classes, two predictors and folds = 2, NNS.stack takes 1.3 s and NNS.boost 1.3 s at n = 1000 (0.9 s and 0.12 s before), and 5.8 s and 8.0 s at n = 5000 (2.6 s and 1.2 s before).
  • Gravity retains its location blend with corrected quartiles and observed bin centers. Mode retains distinct continuous and class behavior. Changes to these defaults can affect regression, optimization, and forecasts.

Forecasting and scenarios

  • ARMA validation support is selected from training observations only. Nonlinear shrinkage follows the same intended mean blend as linear shrinkage, and a single shrunk lag refits recursively. Long-horizon runtime and path bands can therefore differ from earlier releases.
  • The optimizer’s objective describes its returned internal validation forecast. NNS.ARMA.optim no longer adds the gravity bias shift by default (bias.correction = "none"). The former rule estimated the shift on the validation window and accepted it whenever it improved the objective on that same window; it is removed. On rolling-origin forecasts of nine series the shift made held-out MASE worse on eight, under the former rule and under bias.correction = "split", which estimates it on the first half of the window and accepts it on the second and remains an option. Base-model tuning still requires independent outer evaluation. Raw/corrected forecasts and bias metadata are available for assessment.
  • NNS.ARMA.optim and the nonlinear NNS.ARMA methods run faster. The nonlinear step’s weighted rise and run were means of a vector about k^3/3 long for k regression points; they are now computed in closed form, which agrees with the former value to rounding. The optimizer computes each validation forecast once, partitions no longer build their data frames through R, and small partial-moment kernels run on the calling thread; these leave results bit-identical. On a synthetic monthly series of 8000 observations the optimizer took 13 s, against 126 s in 13.3 and 210 s before this change; the AirPassengers example takes 0.10 s, against 0.30 s and 0.39 s.
  • VAR keeps its two-stage forecast design and uses prefix-generated predictors for chronological validation by default. validation = "observed" is the compatibility option. Known contemporaneous outcomes and imputed future targets are not used as deployment-validation inputs or ground truth.
  • NNS.seas reports the fundamental period as best.period: the smallest period that divides the lowest-scoring lag (or nearly divides it, for a non-integer period) and scores within two jackknife standard errors of it, from paired delete-one differences. The lowest score often fell on a multiple of the true period; a monthly sine with noise now returns 12 instead of 36 to 108, and NNS.ARMA’s automatic lag follows. The period is listed first in all.periods and periods. NNS.ARMA does not run the permutation test; pass NNS.seas(x, p.value = TRUE)$best.period as seasonal.factor for a significance-filtered lag.
  • Seasonality adds absolute dispersion for interval-scale data while retaining the historical automatic CV/Gini default. Selected predictive periods need not be fundamental physical periods; permutation interpretations require an appropriate null.
  • Monte Carlo exponent grids stay within requested bounds and reject invalid exponents. Constant/singleton superiority groups and exactly zero bootstrap residuals are handled explicitly. Bootstrap residual expansion is separately configurable. The default forced-mean scale is an iid reference, not a universal serial-dependence uncertainty calibration.

Numerical, documentation, and reproducibility repairs

  • Fix mixed-degree co-partial moments, validate paired lengths before native parallel work, and make integer-degree VaR root stopping scale invariant.
  • Fix target hazard evaluation, stochastic-dominance cluster ordering, residual clusters, efficient-set order dependence, and caller column-name mutation.
  • Replace unsupported example rankings and inference claims with explicit targets and corrected executable workflows. Forecast examples reserve test outcomes; fitted-contrast uncertainty includes model refitting. Add revised editable companions for the historical PDFs, preserve originals, and record that the original editable sources were not recovered.
